# Safety Alert: Synthetic pump fire, 2024

**Grade: Alert**

**DRAFT**

*About 1 min read*

**Audience:** Other sites and peer organisations

**Incident:** Synthetic pump fire · 2024-03-20

## Bottom line

- A pump went back into service after a seal change without a leak test, and the seal failed. [FND-0001; EVD-0001] *(learning: LR-01)*

## What happened

A transfer pump was restarted after a seal change with no leak test on the work order [EVD-0001]. The seal had been bought locally without a specification, and it leaked and caught fire [FND-0003].

## Why it matters to you

Any site that restarts pumps after maintenance without a return-to-service checklist can repeat this [FND-0002].

## What we learned

**Learning:** If a joint is disturbed, test it before service: an untested joint can leak at the first restart. [FND-0001; FND-0002; EVD-0001]

*(learning: LR-01)*

## What to check now

- [ ] **Hold point:** Does every restart after seal work need a signed leak-test record? [FND-0002]
- [ ] Are pump seals bought to a written specification? [FND-0003; EVD-0003]

## Questions for your crew

**Q: When did a pump last go back into service here without a test?** [FND-0001]
- Why it matters: Shows whether the test is part of the job or depends on memory.

**Q: What would you do if the test rig was not available?** [FND-0002]
- Why it matters: Shows whether people feel able to stop a restart.

## Who to contact

Questions about this alert go to the site reliability lead.
